decorative.description: Whether screen readers skip the object as decoration. A decorative shape's words and a decorative chart's labels are skipped too. Without `alt`, an image, video, web video, model, icon, or chart that isn't decorative causes a warning once it has something to show. A counter doesn't, since screen readers read its figure.

anyOf.description: Copies of the object. Each is moved, turned, scaled, and delayed a little more than the one before. The original stays as written. The defaults are 1 for `scale` and `end-opacity`, the center for `anchor-point`, and 0 for the other optional numbers.

repeater.description: Copies of the object. Each is moved, turned, scaled, and delayed a little more than the one before.

start-on.description: With `cue`, the video, audio, or web video starts at a `play` cue. With `slide`, it starts once the transition into its slide has ended, or as the step that first shows it plays. No `play` cue starts it then.

loop.description: With `repeat`, the video or audio plays again from the start of its `media-trim` each time it ends. Without it, it plays once. A video then holds the frame where it stops.

volume.description: How loud the video or audio plays. 1 is the file's own level.

anyOf.description: How long a video's sound takes to rise linearly from silence each time the part set by `media-trim` starts to play. Its picture doesn't fade. It is in seconds.

audio-fade-in.description: How long a video's sound takes to rise linearly from silence each time the part set by `media-trim` starts to play. Its picture doesn't fade.

anyOf.description: How long a video's sound takes to fall linearly to silence before that part ends each time. Where the two fades overlap, the lower volume is used. It is in seconds.

audio-fade-out.description: How long a video's sound takes to fall linearly to silence before that part ends each time. Where the two fades overlap, the lower volume is used.

anyOf.description: The part of the video or audio file that plays: a start and an end in seconds into the file. The part of a video or audio file, or of a clip's Action, that plays.

media-trim.description: The part of the video or audio file that plays: a start and an end in seconds into the file.

anyOf.description: The file path of an image the video shows before it plays. Without it, a video shows the frame at `poster-time`, and a web video its provider's image. A video's override of either key replaces both. It is a file path in the theme's folder, not hidden, not manifest.json, and not in previews or example.

poster.description: The file path of an image the video shows before it plays. Without it, a video shows the frame at `poster-time`, and a web video its provider's image. A video's override of either key replaces both.

anyOf.description: The time in seconds in the video's file of the frame it shows before it plays when it has no `poster`. The default is the start of its `media-trim`.

poster-time.description: The time in seconds in the video's file of the frame it shows before it plays when it has no `poster`. The default is the start of its `media-trim`.

shape-type.description: Which shape a shape object draws. An edit that changes it, other than a step, drops each key the new kind doesn't take.

anyOf.description: How many points a star has.

point-count.description: How many points a star has.

anyOf.description: Where a speech bubble's tail ends. It is in fractions of its frame. The tip of a speech bubble's tail.

tail.description: Where a speech bubble's tail ends. It is in fractions of its frame.

use-as-mask.description: Whether the shape or path clips the members after it in its group to its outline.

anyOf.description: The path's outline: SVG path data where 0 to 1 spans the object's frame.

geometry.description: The path's outline: SVG path data where 0 to 1 spans the object's frame.

fill-rule.description: Which areas of a self-crossing path the fill covers, and the path clips to as a mask.

anyOf.description: The drawn part of the stroke: a start and an end along its length. The drawn part of a path's or a line's stroke.

trim.description: The drawn part of the stroke: a start and an end along its length.

icon.description: The name of the Lucide 1.46.0 icon the object draws. It is the icon's own name, not an alias. A later version never drops a name.

anyOf.description: Where a line starts: a point, or an object it stays attached to. A line end attached to an object.
Where a line starts: a point, or an object it stays attached to.

start.description: Where a line starts: a point, or an object it stays attached to.

anyOf.description: Where a line ends: a point, or an object it stays attached to. A line end attached to an object.
Where a line ends: a point, or an object it stays attached to.

end.description: Where a line ends: a point, or an object it stays attached to.

connection.description: How a line runs between its ends: straight, curved, or elbow. An elbow line turns at right angles halfway between them.

anyOf.description: How far a curved line's middle bends from straight in fractions of the straight distance between its ends. A positive bend goes right, seen from the start toward the end. It is in end-to-end distances.

bend.description: How far a curved line's middle bends from straight in fractions of the straight distance between its ends. A positive bend goes right, seen from the start toward the end.

cap-start.description: What the start of the line shows.

cap-end.description: What the end of the line shows.

chart-type.description: Which chart the object draws: columns or bars per category, side by side or stacked; a line or a stacked area per series; a pie or a donut of the first series; or a counter of the first value.

progress.description: How far the chart has grown in. A counter counts from 0 up to its value as it rises.

delivery.description: How the chart's elements grow. With `by-element`, they grow one after another as `progress` rises. Without it, all grow at once.

anyOf.description: With `delivery`, how many intervals each element grows for. Without `delivery`, it is ignored.

spread.description: With `delivery`, how many intervals each element grows for. Without `delivery`, it is ignored.

digits.description: How a counter's digits reach each value as it grows. With `change`, each digit changes in place. With `roll`, the digits roll into place like an odometer's.

value-labels.description: Where the chart shows each value: `none`, or `auto`, past a bar's or a column's end, above or below a point, or inside a slice, a stacked segment, or a stacked area.

legend.description: Where the chart shows a legend: `none`, or `top`, across the top of the chart. It names a pie's or a donut's categories, or any other chart's series.

series-colors.description: The colors of the chart's series in order. Every chart but a pie, a donut, or a counter uses them. For a `null` or missing entry, the chart uses the slide's color there.

category-colors.description: The colors of the chart's categories in order, one for each slice of a pie or a donut. For a `null` or missing entry, the chart uses the slide's color there.

leading-zero-opacity.description: The opacity of a rolling counter's unused leading zeros: those ahead of its number and of the whole digits its cell writes. Without `digits: roll`, it is ignored.

anyOf.description: How long the audio takes to rise linearly from silence each time the part set by `media-trim` starts to play. It is in seconds.

fade-in.description: How long the audio takes to rise linearly from silence each time the part set by `media-trim` starts to play.

anyOf.description: How long the audio takes to fall linearly to silence before that part ends each time. Where the two fades overlap, the lower volume is used. It is in seconds.

fade-out.description: How long the audio takes to fall linearly to silence before that part ends each time. Where the two fades overlap, the lower volume is used.

url.description: The address of a YouTube or Vimeo video in a form listed below. An override's url replaces the whole video. A web video's `poster` changes only with it.

anyOf.description: Where the object is in the 3D space. Y is up. It places a model's origin, or the center of a light, the camera, or a shadow catcher. A floor's position is its height. It is written as y. A point in the 3D space in canvas units. The x axis runs right from the slide's left edge, the y axis runs up from its bottom edge, and the z axis runs toward the viewer. The slide is at z 0. The axes are right-handed. glTF and three.js use the same axes. After Effects' y and z axes run the other way. A parented object's position is in its parent's space.

Where the object is in the 3D space. Y is up. It places a model's origin, or the center of a light, the camera, or a shadow catcher. A floor's position is its height. It is written as y. A floor's height in the 3D space. A floor is level and goes on without end. So a floor's position has only y. Like a shadow catcher, a floor shows only the shadows cast on it and hides the 3D objects behind it. Without a position, the floor is at the slide's bottom edge.

position.description: Where the object is in the 3D space. Y is up. It places a model's origin, or the center of a light, the camera, or a shadow catcher. A floor's position is its height. It is written as y.

rotation-mode.description: The form of a 3D object's rotation. Without it, the rotation is in degrees in Cinema 4D's HPB order. With `quaternion`, it is written as w, x, y, and z in its space's axes.

anyOf.description: The name of the node in the parent model that a model, a light, a shadow catcher, or the camera moves with. Without it, the object moves with the whole model. It is the name of one of the model's nodes.

parent-node.description: The name of the node in the parent model that a model, a light, a shadow catcher, or the camera moves with. Without it, the object moves with the whole model.

parent-inverse.description: What kept the object in place when it was parented. It has 16 numbers, column by column. Its fourth row is 0, 0, 0, and 1: its 4th, 8th, and 12th numbers are 0, and its 16th is 1.

anyOf.description: The camera lens's focal length in millimeters.

focal-length.description: The camera lens's focal length in millimeters.

anyOf.description: How far in canvas units the camera's lens is shifted up. Cinema 4D's Film Offset Y, Maya's Vertical Film Offset, and Blender's Shift Y shift a lens the same way. The camera doesn't turn. Its lens's axis shows that far below the picture's middle. The default position's y is that much lower. A level camera whose position leaves out y and z then shows z 0 where the slide lays it out. With a negative shift it stands higher and sees the floor from above. With y set, only the lens shifts. A camera with a point of interest turns just enough to show that point at the picture's middle. The default is minus a quarter of the slide's height. A level camera then shows its horizon a quarter of the way down. Write 0 for a camera that stands at the slide's middle.

lens-shift.description: How far in canvas units the camera's lens is shifted up. Cinema 4D's Film Offset Y, Maya's Vertical Film Offset, and Blender's Shift Y shift a lens the same way. The camera doesn't turn. Its lens's axis shows that far below the picture's middle. The default position's y is that much lower. A level camera whose position leaves out y and z then shows z 0 where the slide lays it out. With a negative shift it stands higher and sees the floor from above. With y set, only the lens shifts. A camera with a point of interest turns just enough to show that point at the picture's middle. The default is minus a quarter of the slide's height. A level camera then shows its horizon a quarter of the way down. Write 0 for a camera that stands at the slide's middle.

anyOf.description: The camera's motion blur. The 3D layer blurs along its motion while the shutter is open. Nothing else is blurred. Only exported movies and the Agent's renders show it. A frame is a sixtieth of a second, a movie's frame. The Agent's renders use the same frame at any `sampleRate`.

shutter.description: How long the shutter stays open in frames. At 0, there is no blur. The default is 0.5. It can be animated.

shutter-position.description: Where the frame's moment falls in the shutter's opening: at its start, its center, or its end. The default is center.

samples.description: How many moments the 3D layer is drawn at while the shutter is open. The drawings are then averaged. Cinema 4D's Sub-Frame Motion Blur Samples work the same way. The default is 32.

motion-blur.description: The camera's motion blur. The 3D layer blurs along its motion while the shutter is open.

anyOf.description: The slide's render settings, kept on its camera beside motion blur: a fast estimate of light bouncing between surfaces, and of the World's light blocked where surfaces meet. In Cinema 4D's Render Settings, they are Global Illumination and Ambient Occlusion. The effects show wherever the 3D layer shows. Only surfaces in view bounce light. A shadow catcher or a floor bounces none. An override replaces the whole record.

global-illumination.description: Whether lit surfaces bounce their light onto what is near them. The default is false.

ambient-occlusion.description: Whether the World's light darkens where surfaces close in on each other. A shadow catcher or a floor then also darkens where an object rests on it. The default is false.

distance.description: How far bounced light and shading reach from a surface. The default is 400. It is in canvas units.

render-effects.description: The slide's render settings, kept on its camera beside motion blur: a fast estimate of light bouncing between surfaces, and of the World's light blocked where surfaces meet.

anyOf.description: The camera's drift. As the slide appears, the camera moves from an offset to its set position. It comes to rest there when the drift's duration ends. Its offset is in canvas units along the slide's 3D axes. After animation, parenting, and constraints place the camera, the offset is added to its position and its point of interest. A parent's rotation and scale don't change it. The drift runs on the slide's own clock. That clock starts when the slide's transition in begins. It runs on through the slide's steps, waits, and transition out. While t is less than `duration`, the added offset at t seconds on that clock is `offset` × (1 − t ÷ `duration`)². The offset decreases to zero at `duration` and stays zero afterward. Stills and the editor show the camera without its drift. A slide has no drift when a scroll or carry-over transition enters or leaves it. When a presentation shows two or more slides, the last one's transition counts as entering the first. It does so in a show that stops after its last slide too. A drift on such a slide causes a `drift-with-joining-transition` warning.

offset.description: Where the camera starts: an {x, y, z} offset from its set position. A point in the 3D space in canvas units. The x axis runs right from the slide's left edge, the y axis runs up from its bottom edge, and the z axis runs toward the viewer. The slide is at z 0. The axes are right-handed. glTF and three.js use the same axes. After Effects' y and z axes run the other way. A parented object's position is in its parent's space.

duration.description: How many seconds after the slide begins to appear the camera comes to rest.

drift.description: The camera's drift. As the slide appears, the camera moves from an offset to its set position. It comes to rest there when the drift's duration ends.

point-of-interest.description: The point the camera or a directional, spot, or area light faces. It is used in place of the rotation. It is in the position's space. The camera's or light's top stays toward the top of that space.

anyOf.description: A constraint that moves the slide's camera with an object. Cinema 4D's Position constraint works the same way. Only the camera can have it. With a spring, the camera follows on a spring with that response and damping ratio. It trails a sudden move, catches up, and settles as the object stops. If the spring is still moving 10 seconds after what it follows has stopped, the camera halts where it got to. It stops short of its target. It stays there until a click moves what it follows again. Every key except `id`, `type`, and `target` can be left out.

id.description: The constraint's id, such as follow. It is unique among the camera's constraints. A step animates its strength as `constraints.follow.strength`. It is an id, such as "look".

target.description: The id of the model or light the camera follows. It is an object's id.

target-node.description: The node of the target's model the camera follows: the name of one of the model's nodes, such as ball. The camera follows the node as the model's Action moves it. Without it, the camera follows the target's origin.

axes.description: A list of one or more of the 3D space's axes the camera follows on, such as `["x"]`. Each axis is listed once. The axes can be in any order. Without it, the camera follows on all three.

relative-to-target.description: Whether the camera follows the target at an offset: its own offset from the slide's center at z 0, added to the target's point. With false, it is at the target's point. The default is true.

strength.description: How far the camera moves to the point it follows: 0 is not at all and 1 is fully. The default is 1. It can be animated.

spring.description: The spring the camera follows on. It has the `damping-ratio` and `response` of a keyframe's `spring` interpolation. Without it, the camera follows exactly. The spring the camera follows its target on. It is in the camera's Position constraint. It is written the same way as a keyframe's spring interpolation. Both keys are required.

damping-ratio.description: How strongly the spring is damped. At 1, it is critically damped. Less damping swings further.

response.description: The spring's natural period. A shorter response catches up sooner. It is in seconds.

constraints.description: A model's or the camera's constraints in order. A model's constraints apply after its parent places it, and a node's as the node is posed. An override replaces the list. Their strengths animate.

shape.description: An area light's shape: a rectangle or a disc, `size.x` wide and `size.y` tall. In Redshift's Area Light, they are Rectangle and Disc.

light-type.description: What kind of light it is. A `directional` light shines from one direction, a `spot` in a cone from a point, a `point` every way from a point, and an `area` from a flat shape.

anyOf.description: How bright a light or the World is. For a point, spot, or area light, it is in watts. For a directional light or the World, the color is multiplied by it.

intensity.description: How bright a light or the World is. For a point, spot, or area light, it is in watts. For a directional light or the World, the color is multiplied by it.

anyOf.description: How wide a spot light's cone opens: its full angle in degrees.

cone-angle.description: How wide a spot light's cone opens: its full angle in degrees.

anyOf.description: How far in from a spot light's cone edge its light fades out. It is in degrees. 0 is a hard edge. The default is a quarter of the cone angle. Past half the cone angle, it fades over the whole cone.

falloff-angle.description: How far in from a spot light's cone edge its light fades out. It is in degrees. 0 is a hard edge. The default is a quarter of the cone angle. Past half the cone angle, it fades over the whole cone.

anyOf.description: How soft a spot or point light's shadows are: the light's radius in canvas units. 0 makes crisp shadows.

light-radius.description: How soft a spot or point light's shadows are: the light's radius in canvas units. 0 makes crisp shadows.

anyOf.description: How soft a directional light's shadows are: the full angle in degrees its light comes from. The sun's disc spans about half a degree. 0 makes crisp shadows.

light-angle.description: How soft a directional light's shadows are: the full angle in degrees its light comes from. The sun's disc spans about half a degree. 0 makes crisp shadows.

anyOf.description: An area light's size along its own axes in canvas units. In Redshift's Area Light, they are Size X and Size Y.

size.description: An area light's size along its own axes in canvas units.

anyOf.description: The color of the shadows a shadow catcher or a floor shows: a color role or a hex color without alpha, such as "#000000". A role's alpha is ignored. The shadows' opacity is set by `opacity`.

shadow-color.description: The color of the shadows a shadow catcher or a floor shows: a color role or a hex color without alpha, such as "#000000". A role's alpha is ignored. The shadows' opacity is set by `opacity`.

anyOf.description: A shadow catcher's size along its own x in canvas units. A shadow catcher is a plane that shows only the shadows cast on it and hides the 3D objects behind it.

width.description: A shadow catcher's size along its own x in canvas units. A shadow catcher is a plane that shows only the shadows cast on it and hides the 3D objects behind it.

anyOf.description: A shadow catcher's size in canvas units along its own z when it lies flat, or along its own y when it is a wall.

height.description: A shadow catcher's size in canvas units along its own z when it lies flat, or along its own y when it is a wall.

orientation.description: Which way a shadow catcher faces when it isn't turned. With `y`, it lies flat and faces up. With `z`, it is a wall that faces the viewer. This matches Cinema 4D's Plane Orientation.

environment.description: The map that lights the 3D layer when the World has no color. The map's light is multiplied by the World's `intensity`. The World's `intensity` is 0 unless it is set. Each map is a file the format publishes. It doesn't change a World with a color.

anyOf.description: How far the World's map is turned about the y axis in degrees. It turns the way a 3D object's rotation y turns the object. It doesn't change a World with a color.

environment-rotation.description: How far the World's map is turned about the y axis in degrees. It turns the way a 3D object's rotation y turns the object. It doesn't change a World with a color.

overrides.description: Changes to the master's objects on this layout by id. An object set to `null` is removed. The camera and the World can't be removed.

anyOf.description: an object's id

One object on a slide, a layout, or a master. Its keys depend on its type. A chart type or a shape kind in parentheses, as in chart (counter) or shape (star), is the one that uses the key. Every chart or shape can hold it, and another kind ignores it. Light types in parentheses, as in light (spot, point), are the only ones that take the key. An override needs none of the required keys. The object it changes already has them. In an override, a key set to null removes what the object inherits for that key. The key's default then shows.

frame.description: The object's position and size on the slide in canvas units. An object's position and size in canvas units from the top left of its slide. A table's and an audio object's frame has only x and y: their contents or an icon give them their size. A text box's frame leaves out each side that grows to fit its text. An audio object's frame is the top left of its icon. The icon shows only while editing. It has the same size at any zoom.

z.description: How far in canvas units a text with a 3D `model` is in front of the slide. Without `model`, it is ignored. A model, light, camera, or shadow catcher is at its position's z.

anyOf.description: The color of the text, icon, light, or World, or the single color of an SVG image. Text, shapes, and charts can use a gradient. A light's or the World's takes no alpha: a role's is ignored. It is a color role or a hex color.

The color of the text, icon, light, or World, or the single color of an SVG image. Text, shapes, and charts can use a gradient. A light's or the World's takes no alpha: a role's is ignored. A linear or radial gradient.

color.description: The color of the text, icon, light, or World, or the single color of an SVG image. Text, shapes, and charts can use a gradient. A light's or the World's takes no alpha: a role's is ignored.

auto-size.description: Which sides of the text box grow to fit the text. The text never shrinks. A box set to grow can't animate its size or its text's layout, even on a path. InDesign's Auto-Size works the same way.

min-height.description: The minimum height of a text box that grows in height in canvas units. The box is as tall as its text or this, whichever is taller. The text is placed inside it by its vertical alignment.

column-count.description: The number of text columns. A column is at least 0 wide.

column-gutter.description: The space between text columns. It is in canvas units.

text-path.description: The path the text follows: SVG path data where 0 to 1 spans the object's frame. Motion's Path layout method works the same way.

path-offset.description: How far the point its `align` holds the text at moves along its path.

anyOf.description: A drop shadow behind the object, or none. On a text, its lengths are in ems of the font size. A text's drop shadow. Its keys work like those of Photoshop's Drop Shadow. Its lengths are in ems of the text's font size. First, the text's letters and outline grow solid by size × spread. Then it is blurred by a Gaussian whose standard deviation is size × (1 − spread) / √6. The size isn't a blur radius.

size.description: How far the shadow reaches beyond the text's letters and outline. Photoshop's Size works the same way. It is in ems.

spread.description: The fraction of the size that is solid. The rest of the size is blurred. At 1, the shadow is solid all the way out. Photoshop's Spread works the same way. The default is 0.

offset.description: How far the shadow falls: {x, y} across and down in the text's own axes. It turns and scales with the text and its groups.

color.description: Its color: a color role or a hex color without alpha, such as "#000000". A role's alpha is ignored. The shadow's opacity is set by `opacity` alone.

drop-shadow.description: A drop shadow behind the object, or none. On a text, its lengths are in ems of the font size.

frame.description: The object's position and size on the slide in canvas units. An object's position and size in canvas units from the top left of its slide. A table's and an audio object's frame has only x and y: their contents or an icon give them their size. A text box's frame leaves out each side that grows to fit its text. An audio object's frame is the top left of its icon. The icon shows only while editing. It has the same size at any zoom.

color.description: The color of the text, icon, light, or World, or the single color of an SVG image. Text, shapes, and charts can use a gradient. A light's or the World's takes no alpha: a role's is ignored. It is a color role or a hex color.

column-widths.description: The width of each of a table's columns in order. The table is as wide as its columns. A column past the end of the list is 240 wide. With no list, every column is 240 wide.

min-row-heights.description: The minimum height of each row. A row is taller when its words need more. A row of 0, or one past the list, has no minimum and is as tall as its words. The table is as tall as its rows.

header-row.description: Whether the table's first row is styled as a header.

header-column.description: Whether the table's first column is styled as a header.

alternating-rows.description: Whether every other row is shaded.

gridlines.description: Which of the table's lines show: none, those between rows with the top and bottom edges, or every line with all four edges.

anyOf.description: The file the object shows or plays, such as a model's GLB. It is a presentation's or a theme's file path. A master's or a layout's own image, video, audio, or model that isn't a placeholder can list one file for each color scheme. It is a file path in the theme's folder, not hidden, not manifest.json, and not in previews or example.

The file the object shows or plays, such as a model's GLB. It is a presentation's or a theme's file path. A master's or a layout's own image, video, audio, or model that isn't a placeholder can list one file for each color scheme. A theme object's file for each color scheme. A dark scheme can then use a file of its own. An image, video, audio, or model object can have a file map in place of a single file. Every file in the map is the same type. A placeholder has one file, not a map.

file.description: The file the object shows or plays, such as a model's GLB. It is a presentation's or a theme's file path. A master's or a layout's own image, video, audio, or model that isn't a placeholder can list one file for each color scheme.

color.description: The color of the text, icon, light, or World, or the single color of an SVG image. Text, shapes, and charts can use a gradient. A light's or the World's takes no alpha: a role's is ignored. It is a color role or a hex color.

exposure.description: How much lighter or darker the image is. It is CSS's `brightness()` of 2 to the power of `exposure` on the sRGB values. 0 leaves it unchanged.

contrast.description: How much more or less contrast the image has. After `exposure`, it is CSS's `contrast()` of 1 + `contrast` on the sRGB values. 0 leaves it unchanged.

saturation.description: How much more or less saturated the image's colors are. After `contrast`, it is CSS's `saturate()` of 1 + `saturation` on the sRGB values. 0 leaves them unchanged.

temperature.description: How much warmer or cooler the image's colors are. After `saturation`, red is multiplied by 1 + `temperature` ÷ 4 and blue by 1 − `temperature` ÷ 4. 0 leaves them unchanged.

mask.description: The shape the image is cut to: SVG path data where 0 to 1 spans the frame. It is filled by the nonzero rule.

anyOf.description: The file the object shows or plays, such as a model's GLB. It is a presentation's or a theme's file path. A master's or a layout's own image, video, audio, or model that isn't a placeholder can list one file for each color scheme. It is a file path in the theme's folder, not hidden, not manifest.json, and not in previews or example.

The file the object shows or plays, such as a model's GLB. It is a presentation's or a theme's file path. A master's or a layout's own image, video, audio, or model that isn't a placeholder can list one file for each color scheme. A theme object's file for each color scheme. A dark scheme can then use a file of its own. An image, video, audio, or model object can have a file map in place of a single file. Every file in the map is the same type. A placeholder has one file, not a map.

light.description: The file for the light scheme, and for other light schemes without their own. It is a file path in the theme's folder, not hidden, not manifest.json, and not in previews or example.

dark.description: The file for the dark scheme, and for other dark schemes without their own. It is a file path in the theme's folder, not hidden, not manifest.json, and not in previews or example.

Between two quaternion keyframes, the object turns the shorter way round.

A constraint that turns a model, or one of its nodes, toward a target. Cinema 4D's Aim constraint works the same way. Every key except `id`, `type`, and `target` can be left out.

id.description: The constraint's id, such as look. It is unique among the model's constraints. A step animates its strength as `constraints.look.strength`. It is an id, such as "look".

node.description: The node that turns: the name of one of the model's nodes, such as Head. Without it, the whole model turns.

target.description: The id of the model or light it turns toward. With `camera`, it turns toward the camera. It is an object's id.

target-node.description: The node of the target's model it turns toward: the name of one of the model's nodes, such as Hand. It turns toward the node as the model's Action moves it. Without it, it turns toward the target's origin.

axis.description: The axis of the model or node that points at the target in its GLB's axes. In those axes, y is up, and a model faces along +z. The default is z.

strength.description: How far it turns toward the target: 0 is not at all and 1 is fully. It applies to the result of the constraints before it. The default is 1. It can be animated.

anyOf.description: A constraint that keeps a model's volume as the model scales along its own axes. The volume is measured at the model's `scale` as the object sets it, before any `initial` value or step. An axis it scales stops at a 3D scale's most, 1 × 10¹⁸ either way, and an axis at 0 stays at 0. Every key except `id` and `type` can be left out.

id.description: The constraint's id, such as squash. It is unique among the model's constraints. A step animates its strength as `constraints.squash.strength`. It is an id, such as "look".

mode.description: When the volume is kept, as in Blender's Maintain Volume constraint. With `strict`, it always is. With `uniform`, it is kept while the model scales evenly. With `single-axis`, it is kept while only the free axis scales. The default is strict.

free-axis.description: The axis the constraint leaves as it is. It scales the other two to keep the volume. The default is y.

volume.description: The volume to keep. It is a multiple of the model's volume at its `scale`. The default is 1. At 0.4, the model is squeezed to 40% of its volume. The model's size is its `scale`, not this.

strength.description: How strongly it keeps the volume: 0 is not at all and 1 is fully. The default is 1. It can be animated.

scale.description: How far it is zoomed. At 1, an image fits its frame as its `scale-mode` sets, and a background covers the slide. Above 1, it is zoomed in. Below 1, it is zoomed out.

focal-point.description: The point that stays in view: {x, y}. Each is a fraction of the image, across and down.

based-on.description: What counts as one piece. With `character-and-space`, each space is a piece too. After Effects' Characters is `character-and-space`, and its Characters Excluding Spaces is `character`.

delivery.description: `by-paragraph`: each paragraph enters on the step whose paragraph cue names it. It needs based-on `paragraph` and no seed. Order, spread, pause, and progress must be at their defaults.

duration.description: How long each paragraph takes to enter in seconds. With interpolation hold, it is still required but isn't used. A step that has only paragraphs' cues lasts as long as they take.

from.description: How each piece looks as it starts to enter. A key it leaves out uses the piece's resting value: scale 1, offset x 0, y 0, and rotation and blur 0. Only `opacity` is 0 when left out. Without it, each piece fades in. Motion's Sequence Text with Sequencing From works the same way.

offset.description: How far it starts from where it rests: {x, y} across and down in ems of the piece's own font size. On a path, x is along the path, and y is down from it as its letters stand on it.

scale.description: Its scale. At 1, it is its own size.

rotation.description: How far it is turned in degrees clockwise.

blur.description: How blurred it is: its radius in ems of the piece's own font size.

anyOf.description: How each piece moves into place: gradually, or at once with hold. A text's spring has no `response`, and its elastic has no `period`.

interpolation.description: How each piece moves into place: gradually, or at once with hold. A text's spring has no `response`, and its elastic has no `period`.

fade.description: The fraction of each piece's entrance its fade lasts. The fade starts with the move and follows the piece's interpolation.

order.description: The order the pieces enter in. With a seed, it must be `random`.

seed.description: The seed for a random order: the same seed gives the same order. The default is 0.

spread.description: How many intervals each piece moves for. In forward, backward, or random order, this many pieces move at once.

pause.description: How many intervals the text waits between turns. `enter` says how they count.

progress.description: How far the text has entered. It is animated by steps. It isn't animated when the entrance has a `delivery`.

based-on.description: What counts as one piece. With `character-and-space`, each space is a piece too. After Effects' Characters is `character-and-space`, and its Characters Excluding Spaces is `character`.

to.description: How each piece looks as it finishes exiting. A key it leaves out uses the piece's resting value: scale 1, offset x 0, y 0, and rotation and blur 0. Only `opacity` is 0 when left out. Without it, each piece fades out. Motion's Sequence Text with Sequencing To works the same way.

offset.description: How far it ends from where it rests: {x, y} across and down in ems of the piece's own font size. On a path, x is along the path, and y is down from it as its letters stand on it.

scale.description: Its scale. At 1, it is its own size.

rotation.description: How far it is turned in degrees clockwise.

blur.description: How blurred it is: its radius in ems of the piece's own font size.

anyOf.description: How each piece moves out of place: gradually, or at once with hold. A text's spring has no `response`, and its elastic has no `period`.

interpolation.description: How each piece moves out of place: gradually, or at once with hold. A text's spring has no `response`, and its elastic has no `period`.

fade.description: The fraction of each piece's exit its fade lasts. The fade ends with the move and follows the piece's interpolation.

order.description: The order the pieces exit in. With a seed, it must be `random`.

seed.description: The seed for a random order: the same seed gives the same order. The default is 0.

spread.description: How many intervals each piece moves for. In forward, backward, or random order, this many pieces move at once.

pause.description: How many intervals the text waits between turns. `enter` says how they count.

progress.description: How far the text has exited. It is animated by steps.

light.description: The file for the light scheme, and for other light schemes without their own. It is a file path in the theme's folder, not hidden, not manifest.json, and not in previews or example.

dark.description: The file for the dark scheme, and for other dark schemes without their own. It is a file path in the theme's folder, not hidden, not manifest.json, and not in previews or example.

additionalProperties.description: a file path in the theme's folder, not hidden, not manifest.json, and not in previews or example

y.description: How far up from the slide's bottom edge in canvas units.

frame.height.description: The height. It is in canvas units.

frame.width.description: The width. It is in canvas units.

frame.x.description: How far across the left edge is. When a text box's width grows, it is the point the text is aligned to. It is in canvas units.

frame.y.description: How far down the top edge is. When a text box's height grows, its default `anchor-point` is on its top edge. It is in canvas units.

angle.description: A linear gradient's direction in degrees clockwise from up.

line.description: Where a linear gradient's line is in the box the object is drawn at. It turns about its middle by `angle`. By default it crosses the box it spans through its center. It is the same in CSS. The line a linear gradient runs along. It has a middle and a length. They are in the box the object is drawn at, not in the box the gradient spans. A gradient on a shape's words uses the shape's frame.

x.description: The x of its middle in fractions of the box's width. 0 is the left edge, and 1 is the right edge.

y.description: The y of its middle in fractions of the box's height. 0 is the top edge, and 1 is the bottom edge.

length.description: Its length in fractions of the box's diagonal. It is in box diagonals.

center.description: The center of a radial gradient: {x, y}. The point a radial gradient spreads from. It is in the box the object is drawn at. It can be outside that box. A linear gradient's `line` is in the same box. The point doesn't move while a path's outline morphs. A background's box is the slide, and a gradient on a shape's words uses the shape's frame. The gradient reaches the corner of the box it spans that is farthest from its center. CSS's `farthest-corner` works the same way.

x.description: Its x in fractions of the box's width. 0 is the left edge, and 1 is the right edge.

y.description: Its y in fractions of the box's height. 0 is the top edge, and 1 is the bottom edge.

shape.description: With `circle`, a radial gradient is round in any box. Without it, it is an ellipse.

gradient.stops.description: The gradient's two or more colors and their positions.

object.description: The id of the object it attaches to on the same slide. It is an object's id.

side.description: Which side of the object's frame it attaches to. The sides turn with the object's `rotation`, and a flip doesn't change them. With `auto`, it attaches to the side that faces the other end.

object.align.description: The text's horizontal alignment. Where neither the text nor its style sets one, lines align to the side they start on: the right when `text-direction` is `rtl`, else the left. An explicit `left` stays left in right-to-left text. A table's columns take its style's alignment where its Markdown alignment row names none.

object.alt.description: A description of the object that screen readers read aloud. On a shape or a table, they read it before its words. On a chart, they read it in place of its labels. It is one line that isn't blank and has no control characters or line breaks.

object.anchor-point.description: The point an object turns and scales about. 0.5, 0.5 is the center. A group and a text with a 3D `model` also tilt about it. It is in fractions of the box the object is drawn at: its frame; a growing text box's box at the size of its words; a table's box at its columns' widths and its rows' heights; or a group's box. Without one, an object turns and scales about its center. A text box that grows turns and scales about the point its text grows from. Leaving it out is the only way to the default.

object.blend-mode.description: How the object's colors combine with what is under it. Each mode except a group's `pass-through` is the CSS `mix-blend-mode` of that name. The modes are defined in Compositing and Blending Level 1.

object.blur.description: The radius of the object's Gaussian blur in canvas units.

object.bullet-styles.description: The bullet at each list level in order from the first. There is at least one. The last one is used at every deeper level.

object.case.description: The letter case the text is shown in. The text itself stays as typed. With `capitalize`, each word starts with a capital.

object.cast-shadow.description: Whether a model or a text with a 3D `model` casts shadows. On a light, whether it casts the shadows of the models and texts that cast them. A text without `model` ignores it.

object.color.description: The color of the text, icon, light, or World, or the single color of an SVG image. Text, shapes, and charts can use a gradient. A light's or the World's takes no alpha: a role's is ignored. It is a color role or a hex color without alpha, such as "#000000".

object.constrain-proportions.description: Whether the object's scale, or a group's size, keeps its proportions when one side changes.

object.corner-radius.description: How round a rectangle's, an image's, or a video's corners are. An image's or a video's corners are its frame's. A masked image's radius isn't drawn until its mask is removed. It is in canvas units.

object.crop.description: How far the image or video is zoomed inside its frame, and which point stays in view. An image's or a video's zoom inside its frame, and the point that stays in view. The defaults are scale 1 and focal-point 0.5, 0.5.

object.decorative.description: Whether screen readers skip the object as decoration. A decorative shape's words and a decorative chart's labels are skipped too. Without `alt`, an image, video, web video, model, icon, or chart that isn't decorative causes a warning once it has something to show. A counter doesn't, since screen readers read its figure.

anyOf.description: A drop shadow behind the object, or none. On a text, its lengths are in ems of the font size. A drop shadow. Its keys work like those of Photoshop's Drop Shadow. First, what the object paints grows solid by size × spread. Then it is blurred by a Gaussian whose standard deviation is size × (1 − spread) / √6. The size isn't a blur radius.

size.description: How far it reaches in canvas units.

spread.description: The fraction of the size that is solid. The rest of the size is blurred. At 1, the shadow is solid all the way out. Photoshop's Spread works the same way. The default is 0.

offset.description: How far it falls: {x, y} across and down in the object's own axes. It turns and scales with the object and its groups. A flip doesn't mirror it. A background's offset is in the slide's axes.

color.description: Its color: a color role or a hex color without alpha, such as "#000000". A role's alpha is ignored. The shadow's opacity is set by `opacity` alone.

object.drop-shadow.description: A drop shadow behind the object, or none. On a text, its lengths are in ems of the font size.

object.enter.description: Text that enters one paragraph, word, or character at a time. Text that enters piece by piece. `based-on` sets whether a piece is a paragraph, a word, or a character. The defaults are interpolation linear, fade 1, order forward, spread 1, pause 0, and progress 1. With delivery `by-paragraph`, it works as PowerPoint's By Paragraph.

object.exit.description: Text that exits one paragraph, word, or character at a time. Text that exits piece by piece. Its pieces are counted and timed the same way as an entrance's pieces. The defaults are interpolation linear, fade 1, order forward, spread 1, pause 0, and progress 0.

anyOf.description: The paint inside the shape, path, or table cells: a color, a gradient, or none. It is a color role or a hex color.
The paint inside the shape, path, or table cells: a color, a gradient, or none. A linear or radial gradient.

object.fill.description: The paint inside the shape, path, or table cells: a color, a gradient, or none.

object.flip.description: Which way the object's picture, glyph, or outline is mirrored along its own axes: horizontally, vertically, or both. An image's `mask`, a shape's gradients, and a shape's text aren't mirrored.

object.font-family.description: The font role the text uses. The theme sets a font family for each role. A chart's sets every label's font. Keynote's Chart Font works the same way.

object.font-size.description: The font size. It is in canvas units.

object.font-style.description: Whether the text's letters stand upright, `normal`, or lean, `italic`. They lean only in a family with an italic face. Faces, under the master's `fonts`, says which face draws them.

object.font-weight.description: The font weight: 100 thin, 200 extra light, 300 light, 400 regular, 500 medium, 600 semibold, 700 bold, 800 extra bold, or 900 black. Faces, under the master's `fonts`, says which face draws it.

object.frame.description: The object's position and size on the slide in canvas units. An object's position and size in canvas units from the top left of its slide. A table's and an audio object's frame has only x and y: their contents or an icon give them their size. A text box's frame leaves out each side that grows to fit its text. An audio object's frame is the top left of its icon. The icon shows only while editing. It has the same size at any zoom.

object.grayscale.description: How far the colors fade to gray. After `temperature`, it is CSS's `grayscale()` of `grayscale` on the sRGB values. 0 leaves them unchanged.

object.id.description: Its id: an object's id, unique on its slide. Only the camera has the id `camera`, and only the World has the id `world`.

object.inset.description: The space between the edges of a shape or a table cell and its text in canvas units. On a shape, it places the text box, and `padding-top` and `padding-bottom` add space inside that box.

object.intensity.description: How bright a light or the World is. For a point, spot, or area light, it is in watts. For a directional light or the World, the color is multiplied by it.

object.kerning.description: Whether the font's kerning sets the space between letters. With `none`, it works as InDesign's Kerning 0.

object.light-radius.description: How soft a spot or point light's shadows are: the light's radius in canvas units. 0 makes crisp shadows.

object.line-height.description: The distance between lines in multiples of the font size.

object.link.description: Where a click on the object goes while presenting: a webpage, an email address, a phone number, or another slide. The Links section says how each is written.

object.list-indent.description: How far each list level indents. It is in canvas units.

object.locked.description: Whether the object is locked against selection and editing on the canvas.

object.loop.description: With `repeat`, the video or audio plays again from the start of its `media-trim` each time it ends. Without it, it plays once. A video then holds the frame where it stops.

object.media-trim.description: The part of the video or audio file that plays: a start and an end in seconds into the file. The part of a video or audio file, or of a clip's Action, that plays.

object.name.description: The object's name. It is one line that isn't blank and has no control characters or line breaks.

object.number-spacing.description: How wide the digits are. With `default`, each digit has its font's width. With `tabular`, all digits have the same width. Numbers then line up in columns. Word's number spacing works the same way.

object.padding-bottom.description: The space between the text box's last line and its bottom. It is in canvas units.

object.padding-top.description: The space between the text box's top and its first line. It is in canvas units.

object.paragraph-spacing.description: The space between paragraphs. It is in canvas units.

object.parent.description: The id of its group. A group doesn't move its members: their frames and ends stay in the slide's coordinates. A model, a light, a shadow catcher, or the camera moves with its parent model or light. It is an object's id.

object.parent-inverse.description: What kept the object in place when it was parented. It has 16 numbers, column by column. Its fourth row is 0, 0, 0, and 1: its 4th, 8th, and 12th numbers are 0, and its 16th is 1.

object.parent-node.description: The name of the node in the parent model that a model, a light, a shadow catcher, or the camera moves with. Without it, the object moves with the whole model. It is the name of one of the model's nodes.

object.placeholder.description: On a layout's text, image, or video, true makes it a placeholder.

object.point-of-interest.description: The point the camera or a directional, spot, or area light faces. It is used in place of the rotation. It is in the position's space. The camera's or light's top stays toward the top of that space.

object.position.description: Where the object is in the 3D space. Y is up. It places a model's origin, or the center of a light, the camera, or a shadow catcher. A floor's position is its height. It is written as y. A point in the 3D space in canvas units. The x axis runs right from the slide's left edge, the y axis runs up from its bottom edge, and the z axis runs toward the viewer. The slide is at z 0. The axes are right-handed. glTF and three.js use the same axes. After Effects' y and z axes run the other way. A parented object's position is in its parent's space.

object.poster.description: The file path of an image the video shows before it plays. Without it, a video shows the frame at `poster-time`, and a web video its provider's image. A video's override of either key replaces both. It is a file path in the theme's folder, not hidden, not manifest.json, and not in previews or example.

object.repeater.description: Copies of the object. Each is moved, turned, scaled, and delayed a little more than the one before. The original stays as written. The defaults are 1 for `scale` and `end-opacity`, the center for `anchor-point`, and 0 for the other optional numbers.

object.rotation.description: How far a flat object is turned about its `anchor-point` in degrees clockwise. A group's rotation is the angle its box is measured at. A 3D object's rotation is in the form its `rotation-mode` sets.

object.rotation-mode.description: The form of a 3D object's rotation. Without it, the rotation is in degrees in Cinema 4D's HPB order. With `quaternion`, it is written as w, x, y, and z in its space's axes.

object.scale.description: How far the object is stretched along its own axes. It has x and y on a flat object, and x, y, and z on a model or a light. A flat object's scale along its own axes. The object scales about its `anchor-point`. Text breaks into lines first, then stretches with the scale.

object.scale-mode.description: How an image or video fills its frame. With `fill`, it covers the frame and the rest is cropped. With `fit`, all of it shows inside the frame.

object.shadow-color.description: The color of the shadows a shadow catcher or a floor shows: a color role or a hex color without alpha, such as "#000000". A role's alpha is ignored. The shadows' opacity is set by `opacity`.

object.start-on.description: With `cue`, the video, audio, or web video starts at a `play` cue. With `slide`, it starts once the transition into its slide has ended, or as the step that first shows it plays. No `play` cue starts it then.

object.stroke.description: The color of the outline or the line. An image's or a video's outline is its frame's, wherever its picture is in it, and a masked image's follows its mask. A path's stroke can be a gradient. It is a color role or a hex color.

object.stroke-style.description: Whether the outline or the line is solid, dashed, or dotted.

object.stroke-weight.description: How thick the outline or the line is in canvas units. An icon's weight is its line weight in icon units.

object.text-direction.description: Which way every paragraph of the text runs: `ltr`, left to right, or `rtl`, right to left. Arabic and Hebrew use `rtl`. Lists, quotes, and columns start on that side.

object.text-stroke.description: The color of a stroke around each letter. Keynote's text Outline works the same way. It is a color role or a hex color.

object.text-stroke-weight.description: The thickness of the stroke around each letter in ems.

object.text-style.description: The theme text style the object's text uses: a text style name, as in the master's `text-styles`. No name is built in. One the master lacks causes an `unknown-text-style` warning. The text then has none.

object.tilt.description: How far a group or a text with a 3D `model` tilts in depth about its anchor point in degrees. A text without `model` ignores it. How far a group or a text with a 3D `model` tilts in depth about axes through its anchor point in the slide's plane. It is in degrees. A group's picture is seen in perspective from in front of its anchor, through a 50 mm lens, wherever the slide's camera stands. A text's model turns in the slide's 3D space, about its anchor point at its `z`, and the slide's camera sees it there. Its words and their links stand on the turned plane.

object.tracking.description: Extra space between letters. It is in ems.

object.trim.description: The drawn part of the stroke: a start and an end along its length. The drawn part of a path's or a line's stroke.

object.use-as-mask.description: Whether the shape or path clips the members after it in its group to its outline.

object.vertical-align.description: The text's vertical alignment in its box. Text in more than one column always sits at the top.

object.visible.description: Whether the object shows on the slide. A hidden light is off, and a hidden video, web video, or audio object doesn't play. A step can't animate it on an audio object or a light.

object.volume.description: How loud the video or audio plays. 1 is the file's own level.

object.wipe.description: A straight edge that reveals the object as its progress rises from 0 to 1. A reveal behind a moving straight edge. The defaults are progress 1, angle 90, and feather 0.

copies.description: How many copies there are. The original counts as one.

position.description: The move from each copy to the next: {x, y} across and down. It is measured in the turned and scaled axes of the copy before.

rotation.description: How far each copy is turned clockwise from the one before. It is in degrees.

scale.description: How much each copy is scaled from the one before. At 1, each copy is the same size as the one before.

anchor-point.description: The point `rotation` and `scale` turn and scale the copies about: {x, y}. Each is a fraction of the box the object is drawn at, across and down. A group's is the group's box.

stagger.description: How much later each copy plays the object's animation than the one before. A copy can play it up to (copies − 1) × `stagger` + `stagger-randomness` later. Keyframes of the object's own `repeater` aren't delayed: they lay out every copy at once. It is in seconds.

end-opacity.description: The last copy's opacity. It is a fraction of the object's opacity. The copies between fade toward it evenly. After Effects' End Opacity works the same way with a Start Opacity of 100%.

position-randomness.description: The farthest each copy moves in a random direction. It is in canvas units.

rotation-randomness.description: The farthest each copy turns either way at random about its own center. Motion's Replicator Angle Randomness works the same way. It is in degrees.

scale-randomness.description: The most each copy grows or shrinks at random about its own center. It is a fraction of its size.

stagger-randomness.description: The most extra time each copy waits at random. It is in seconds.

seed.description: The random seed: the same seed gives the same copies. Motion's Random Seed works the same way.

x.description: Degrees about x, or a quaternion's x. It is in degrees.

y.description: Degrees about y, or a quaternion's y. It is in degrees.

z.description: Degrees about z, or a quaternion's z. It is in degrees.

x.description: How far across. It is in canvas units.

y.description: How far up. It is in canvas units.

z.description: How far toward the viewer. It is in canvas units.

w.description: A quaternion's w. It is used in quaternion mode only.

x.description: Degrees about x, or a quaternion's x.

y.description: Degrees about y, or a quaternion's y.

z.description: Degrees about z, or a quaternion's z.

color.description: The color: a color role or a hex color.

position.description: Where the color is along the gradient from 0 to 1. A stop is never before the previous one.

x.description: How far across the frame in fractions of its width.

y.description: How far down the frame in fractions of its height.

x.description: It turns about the horizontal axis. With a positive x, its top turns away from the viewer. CSS's `rotateX()` turns the same way. A 3D object's `rotation.x` turns the other way. It is in degrees.

y.description: It turns about the vertical axis. With a positive y, its left side comes forward. The object's rotation comes first, then the y turn, then the x turn. It is in degrees.

start.description: Where it starts in seconds into the file or the Action. The default is 0.

end.description: Where it ends in seconds into the file or the Action. It must come after start. Without it, the file or the Action plays to its end.

start.description: Where the drawn part starts along the stroke in fractions of its length.

end.description: Where the drawn part ends along the stroke in fractions of its length.

progress.description: How far the edge has crossed the object's box along `angle`. At 0, the edge is where the box begins. At 1, its soft edge is past the box's far side. A text's box includes the words that run past it.

angle.description: Which way the edge travels in degrees clockwise from up in the object's own axes. It turns and scales with the object and its groups, and a flip doesn't mirror it.

feather.description: How wide the soft edge is. It is in canvas units along the object's own axes and scales with the object. Across it, the object fades from shown to hidden.
